subject: Post-demo: Stakeholder mapping & next steps for Acme Commerce
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Emma Johnson <emma.johnson@acme-commerce.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: Stakeholder mapping & next steps for Acme Commerce

Hi Emma —

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier today. Quick recap from our side and a couple of requests so we can put together a tailored mutual action plan: 

- What we heard: Primary use case is customer-facing chat on product pages (high QPS unpredictable bursts) + internal search embeddings for support. Latency and cost are the top two decision criteria.
- Questions to unblock procurement & security: can you share the list of people we should loop in for security/compliance (SOC 2/data residency), legal for contract redlines, and procurement for PO/invoicing? Also helpful to know who the economic buyer / final decision maker is (title and email).
- Timeline: you mentioned an internal procurement window in ~3–6 weeks. Is that still accurate? Any blackout dates or budget cycles we should be aware of?

If you can share a quick org chart or a list (names + roles + emails) we’ll draft a short SOW and a pricing anchor for the CFO/economic buyer. Attaching our stakeholder-template would be helpful — I can fill any gaps once you send their names.

Proposed next step: 30-min call next week to introduce procurement/legal and align on SOC 2 evidence they’ll need. I’m available Wed/Thu afternoons PT.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
m: (415) 555-0198
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Emma Johnson <emma.johnson@acme-commerce.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acme-commerce.com>, procurement@acme-commerce.com
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2026 17:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Stakeholder mapping & next steps for Acme Commerce

Hi Marissa —

Great demo — thanks to you and the team. Attaching a high-level org chart (Acme_OrgChart_v2.pdf) and a short mapping below: 

- Economic buyer: Priya Desai, CFO (priya.desai@acme-commerce.com) — will need cost per 1M token scenarios and multi-region pricing.
- Security/Compliance: Liam O'Connor (cc'd) is our Head of Security — primary for SOC 2, data handling, and SSO. He prefers an inventory of evidence (SOC 2 report, data retention policy, KMS details).
- Legal: Julia Martinez, Senior Counsel (julia.martinez@acme-commerce.com) — expect standard redlines around data use and indemnity.
- Procurement: procurement@acme-commerce.com (POs, payment terms). We typically run a 3–6 week procurement cycle for new vendors. This quarter we have a budget decision on July 15.

Notes / constraints: We require SSO + SCIM for user provisioning and a SOC 2 Type II report. Also evaluating a price floor for bursty traffic; any recommendations on burst capacity vs reserved?

Happy to intro you to Priya and Julia if you can share a short one-pager and a pricing anchor and draft SOW.

Thanks,
Emma
Emma Johnson
Head of Product Operations
Acme Commerce
emma.johnson@acme-commerce.com
Attachment: Acme_OrgChart_v2.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Post-demo: Stakeholder mapping & next steps for Acme Commerce

Looping you in — Emma sent an org chart and called out the CFO (Priya Desai) as the economic buyer, plus legal (Julia) and security (Liam). Procurement timeline looks like 3–6 weeks with a budget decision on July 15.

Immediate asks: 
- Rishi: can you prepare a short pricing anchor (cost per 1M tokens; reserved vs burst; recommended quantization tradeoffs) and a bulleted list of what evidence we can provide for Liam (SOC 2, data retention, KMS/HSM info, SSO/SCIM notes)?
- Aditya: can you draft a 1-page SOW template we can send to Priya and Julia with a placeholder for trial capacity and expected QPS? Keep it simple — term, support SLAs, billing.

Goal: get a 1-pager + pricing anchor into Emma by EOD Thu so she can intro us to Priya/Julia ahead of their budget meeting.

Thanks — I’ll draft the intro email once we have the one-pager.

Marissa

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Emma Johnson <emma.johnson@acme-commerce.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, procurement@acme-commerce.com
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Stakeholder mapping & next steps for Acme Commerce

Hi Emma —

Thanks for the quick mapping and org chart — very helpful. Per our internal discussion we attached a short draft SOW and a pricing anchor (summary below) to share with Priya and Julia.

Pricing anchor (high level):
- Trial / PoC: complimentary trial for up to 50k monthly active queries for 30 days.
- Onboarding / Reserved: $XX,000 / month for 4 reserved GPUs (predictable throughput) — includes 99.9% uptime SLA and 24/7 support.
- Burst: pay-as-you-go at $Y per 1k tokens with an optional burst cap to limit monthly spend.
Security evidence we can provide to Liam: SOC 2 Type II report, data retention policy, KMS integration notes, SSO/SCIM setup doc, and a short architecture diagram.
Attached: SOW_draft.docx (placeholder SOW). If that looks good, could you please: 
1) Intro us to Priya Desai and Julia Martinez (short 1-line intros are fine)
2) Confirm whether procurement@acme-commerce.com prefers Net30 / Net45 / PO-first for new vendors
Proposed 30-min intro call Tues 7/6 or Wed 7/7. What works for Priya / Julia?
Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
Attachment: SOW_draft.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)
